continents.fact: Largest and most populous continent; home to the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau, the 'Roof of the World'.
Straddles the equator; the East African Rift is a divergent plate boundary splitting the continent.
The Rocky Mountains and Appalachians frame the interior plains.
The Andes, the longest continental mountain range, run along its western edge above a subduction zone.
Holds about 90% of the world's ice; its average elevation is the highest of any continent.
The Alps were raised by the collision of the African and Eurasian plates.
Australia is the flattest and driest inhabited continent.

topics.d: Earth's lithosphere is broken into about 15 major plates. Their boundaries (shown from the PB2002 model) host most earthquakes and volcanoes. Turn on the Plates layer and the Earthquakes layer together to see the pattern.
Trenches form where one plate subducts beneath another. The deepest, the Mariana Trench, reaches roughly 11 km below sea level.
Major ranges mark collisions (Himalayas, Alps) or subduction (Andes, Rockies). Turn on Mountain highlighting to outline them from Natural Earth data.
Seven continents by the common convention. Tap one to fly there.
The 23.44° axial tilt makes the terminator sweep between the polar circles over a year. Use the Time panel to fast-forward through a solstice.
